MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  March 4, 2013

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Reardon at 5:01 p.m., on March 4, 2013, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on February 27, 2013, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Ury
  Council Member Leckness
  Council Member Schlicht (arrived at 5:03 p.m.)
  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley
  Mayor Reardon

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Reardon

INVOCATION: Council Member Leckness

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Labor Negotiations—The City Council will Provide Direction to its Labor Negotiator
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6. The Parties to the Negotiations are the
  City and the City’s Unrepresented Employees. The City’s Negotiator is Dennis Wilberg

City Council Minutes  1  March 4, 2013
 CS2. Public Employee Performance Evaluation of the Incumbent for the Position of City
  Manager Pursuant to Government Code Sections 54957 and 54957.6

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:02 p.m., Mayor Reardon recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:09 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the City Council received information and gave
direction to staff but there was no reportable action from Closed Session.

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Community of Character Award - Madison Savlov

  Mayor Reardon presented the Community of Character Award to Madison Savlov.

P2. Adopted Headquarters Battalion of the 1st Marine Division Quarterly Recognition

  Mayor Reardon presented certificates of commendation to Marine of the Quarter Lance
  Corporal Brenton T. Rice and Noncommissioned Officer of the Quarter Corporal Steven J.
  Deneus.

P3. Presentation by Goodwill Industries

  The City Council and audience received the presentation from Hal Colebaugh, Veteran
  Services Coordinator, Goodwill Industries.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Bill Ernisse, M.V.: announced that the Wounded Warriors amputee softball games will be held
on Saturday, March 9, 2013, at Marty Russo field #4 on Olympiad Road. The first game starts at
1:00 p.m. and the second game will begin around 2:30 p.m. He extended a special invitation to
the City Council Members and stated that he hopes to see them all there. Lastly, Mr. Ernisse
asked the community to not forget our POWs and MIAs and he stated that freedom is not free.

Joe Holtzman, M.V.: thanked staff members Chuck Wilson and Elaine Lister for creating the
best website on residential solar energy that he has seen. He encouraged residents to consider
solar installation and he announced that Mission Viejo waves permit fees for doing so.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 2, 3, 4, and 8 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.
City Council Minutes  2  March 4, 2013
 Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ury, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and
  further reading waived.

5.  Amendment to Agreement for Building Plan Check and Inspection Services - Charles
  Abbott Associates, Inc.

  Approved the First Amendment of Agreement with Charles Abbott Associates, Inc. for
  Building Plan Check and Inspection Services for the Period from July 1, 2013 to June 30,
  2015.

6.  First Amendment to Agreement for Professional Services for Housing Rehabilitation
  Program - Housing Rehabilitation Consulting Services.

  Approved First Amendment to Agreement with Housing Rehabilitation Consulting
  Services to substitute Lilley Planning Group for Housing Rehabilitation Consulting
  Services.

7.  Safe Routes to School Sidewalk and Curb Ramp Improvements (CIP 211)-Notice of
  Completion

  (1) Certified the completion of and accepted the improvements for the subject project; (2)
  authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City
  Clerk to record the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the
  faithful performance and payment bonds one year and 35 days, respectively, after the date
  of recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being filed
  with the City; and (4) authorized payment of the final retention 35 days after the date of
  recordation of the Notice of Completion.

9.  La Paz Bridge and Road Widening (CIP 756)-Easement Acquisition Agreement

  Approved the easement acquisition agreement with VMA La Paz, LLC, at a cost of
  $177,000.00.

City Council Minutes  3  March 4, 2013
 PUBLIC HEARINGS

10. General Plan Amendment GPA2011-29, being a City-initiated petition to update the
  City’s adopted Housing Element of the General Plan as required by State law. The
  Housing Element consists of housing goals and policies for the City. Specific housing
  programs that will implement these goals and policies are identified. In addition, the
  Housing Element summarizes the City’s existing and projected housing providing the
  basis for targeting policies and programs to address these needs. The goals and
  policies of the draft Housing Element carry forward much from the City’s existing
  Housing Element, with refinements and new programs to address changed
  circumstances and new state laws.

  Director of Community Development Chuck Wilson presented the staff report.

  John Douglas, Planning Consultant, J.H. Douglas & Associates: provided an overview of
  the proposed Housing Element update and noted that there are no major changes before the
  City Council tonight.

  Mayor Reardon opened the public hearing at 7:11 p.m.

  Linda Tang, Kennedy Commission, Irvine: stated that the Kennedy Commission advocates
  for the development of homes affordable to working families. She thanked staff for
  including them as part of this process and she commended the City's leadership for
  addressing affordable housing needs and for implementing this Housing Element.

  At the hour of 7:14 p.m., Mayor Reardon closed the public hearing.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ury, to (1) adopt
  Resolution 13-14 Approving General Plan Amendment GPA2011-29 to Modify the City's
  General Plan Housing Element; and (2) adopt Negative Declaration declaring proposed
  Resolution will not have a significant adverse effect on the environment for purposes of
  CEQA review.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

City Manager’s Report

20. Mid-Year Budget Review for FY 2012/13

City Council Minutes  4  March 4, 2013
   Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report and answered
  the City Council Members questions.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to adopt
  Resolution 13-15 Amending the FY 2012/13 Budget for Adjustments to Certain Revenue
  Sources and Operating and Capital Improvement Program Appropriations.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to adopt
  Resolution 13-16 Updating the City's Authorized Positions and Salary Ranges Schedules
  for Authorized Job Classifications.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

OLD BUSINESS

11. Discussion of Possible Rescission of Ordinance 12-293 Relating to Commercial Real
  Estate Signs

  Director of Community Development Chuck Wilson presented the staff report.

  Michael Valdez, M.V.: stated that the agenda report makes no mention of the campaign that
  he has undertaken to ensure that the newly adopted regulations are enforced by City staff
  and he expressed opposition to the new sign standards.

  Harry Lenczyk, M.V.: submitted a written comment stating that signs should revert back to
  4 square feet unless there is a guarantee that they would never become larger than 16
  square feet.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Leckness, to retain
  the current ordinance as-is.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ury, to move the
  previous question and end the debate.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
City Council Minutes  5  March 4, 2013
   AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, and Ury
  NOES:  Reardon and Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

  On roll call, said MAIN motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS

12. Revision to Investment Policy Regarding Broker-Dealers

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.

  Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: stated that he agrees with the Investment Advisory
  Commission's recommendation to revise the broker-dealer policy and with the
  recommendation to drop UBS from the list of broker-dealers.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Reardon, to maintain the
  current Investment Policy and broker-dealer list.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

13. Appointment to the Orange County Vector Control Board

  Mayor Reardon appointed Council Member Leckness to the Orange County Vector Control
  Board.

14. Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley presented the report.

  Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: discussed recent actions of the OCFA Board and stated that the
  Board should conduct its own investigation into a recent hazing incident. He also
  mentioned the pending transfer of the Hazardous Materials Program to the County Health
  Care Agency and he recommended that the transfer is not made until the District Attorney's
  office concludes its investigation. Mr. Wontrobski further recommended that the OCFA
  Board go back and do an audit of prior years and address runaway spending.

City Council Minutes  6  March 4, 2013
 15. Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Reardon presented the report.

16. San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Reardon presented the report.

17. Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)

  Council Member Ury presented the report.

City Manager’s Report (Continued)

18. Continuation of the slope landscape rehabilitation project along Marguerite Parkway

  City Manager Wilberg noted that staff seeks clarification from the City Council regarding
  the slope rehabilitation along Marguerite Parkway.

  Council Member Schlicht expressed her dissatisfaction that this agenda item is attributed to
  her questions of staff and she stated that all of her votes have been yes votes.

  Mr. Wilberg responded that staff reacted to her emails questioning whether or not they had
  the authority to proceed with rehabilitation further down Marguerite Parkway.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ury, to confirm the
  use of budget slope rehabilitation funds.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

19. Report on Recent Actions of the Successor Agency Oversight Board

  City Manager Wilberg presented the report.

City Attorney’s Report

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that he had nothing to report.

City Council Minutes  7  March 4, 2013
 RECESS

At the hour of 9:01 p.m., Mayor Reardon declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 9:02
p.m. with four City Council Members present. Council Member Kelley departed at 9:03 p.m. and
was absent from the remainder of the City Council Meeting.

NEW BUSINESS

There were no New Business items.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

2.  City Council Minutes

  Council Member Schlicht stated that she feels the Minutes are incomplete under her
  Council Comments and she asked that her entire statement on the annual report be
  included.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, to approve
  the Minutes for regular City Council meeting of February 18, 2013, as amended.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Kelley

3.  Check Register Dated February 8, 2013 in the Amount of $1,207,476.65

  Council Member Schlicht inquired about payments made to Civic Resource Group (CRG.)

  Mayor Reardon read Director Dyas' email summary of the CRG project which includes
  ongoing website development work, a refresh of the City's homepage, the Animal Services
  page and development of a "Things to Do" page. She also addressed history of the firm and
  the kind of work that they do.

  Council Member Schlicht asked staff to describe what a website refresh means and the
  Council requested a response when the information is available. She expressed concern
  with the amount of work being done on vehicles #25 and #177 and asked staff to provide a
  report on the condition of those vehicles. She also inquired about chairs that were
  purchased for the library and whether that was a deposit or the full cost.

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Administrative Services Keith Rattay responded that he
  believes it was the full price of the chairs.

City Council Minutes  8  March 4, 2013
   Mayor Reardon noted that she previously asked for information on a payment made to
  Orange County Transportation for gas tax exchange and she read Director Dyas' email
  response which outlined the exchange agreement with OCTA.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Reardon, to ratify the
  accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Kelley

4.  Check Register dated February 15, 2013 in the amount of $442,912.00

  Council Member Schlicht asked about a payment made to RJM; what professional services
  were required for Veterans Way and what are the irrigation details for the project.

  Director Rattay stated that RJM completed design studies of Veterans Way for a potential
  grant for the Safe Routes to School program. They also completed irrigation details relative
  to the City's drought tolerance ordinance and for a grant application for the Oso Creek
  ramp.

  Council Member Schlicht asked about a payment made for music license fees and
  requested that staff report back on what the music is used for. She also inquired about a fee
  paid to the State Water Resources Board for a dog park application fee.

  Director Rattay responded that large scale plans have to be certified by the State Water
  Resources Board which holds the City accountable.

  Director Dyas responded to questions that Mayor Reardon had posted earlier regarding
  development fees collected by the County for improvements on Avery Parkway. While
  Laguna Niguel took the lead on the project, this city submitted the claim for reimbursement
  since Mission Viejo was under agreement with the County. When reimbursement was
  received, the monies were returned to the City of Laguna Niguel so it was essentially a
  pass-through.

  Mayor Reardon also outlined work done by S. Parker Engineering on the Crown Valley
  Parkway widening project and new electrical service for the irrigation controller.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Leckness, to ratify
  the accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  9  March 4, 2013
   AYES:  Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Kelley

8.  Jeronimo Road Pavement Rehabilitation (CIP 837)-Execution of Funding Agreements

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon presented the staff report and responded to
  Council Member Schlicht's question about the scope of the project changing. Mr. Chagnon
  stated that the change does not affect the grant funding.

  Motion made by Mayor Reardon, seconded by Council Member Ury, to adopt Resolution
  13-13 Approving and Authorizing the City Manager to Enter into Agreements with the
  State Department of Transportation for the Jeronimo Road Pavement Rehabilitation
  Project.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Kelley

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

21. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented
  in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.

Council Member Leckness

Council Member Leckness encouraged his colleagues to watch their words. He stated that he
doesn't like to hear staff accused of wrongdoing and that each Council Member needs to watch
what they say because people are listening. He announced that he attended a variety of opening
day events and the recent DUI Summit at Concordia University where Mayor Pro Tem Kelley
spoke on Mission Viejo's Social Host Ordinance. He also attended the Saddleback College
library re-dedication event and he noted that the improvements are great and it is a phenomenal
facility. Lastly, Council Member Leckness encouraged residents to attend the Wounded Warriors
softball event on Saturday.

Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht announced that she feels the Council made a mistake on allowing the
commercial real estate signs to stay the size that they are. She stated that tenancy isn't increased
by the size of the signs and she feels it's just branding of the real estate company. She outlined
her recent vacation and her attendance at the Rancho Mission Viejo Little League opening day
City Council Minutes  10  March 4, 2013
 event. She also discussed upcoming events including the Chamber of Commerce annual
breakfast at the end of the month and Up in the Air on March 16. Council Member Schlicht
announced that the Chamber's after hours networking event will be held on March 5, 2013, from
5:00 to 7:00 p.m. at Buffalo Wild Wings and she noted that the Chamber is doing a lot of good
for the community. Council Member Schlicht concluded her comments with a quote from Chief
Joseph, "It does not require many words to speak the truth."

Council Member Ury

Council Member Ury announced that he had no comments this evening.

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley was absent.

Mayor Reardon

Mayor Reardon announced that she has responses to questions that resident Joe Holtzman and
Council Member Schlicht posed about check register items at the last meeting. She encouraged
anyone to contact her if they would like a copy of the email. Mayor Reardon announced that she
too attended the DUI Summit event where she heard Supervisor Todd Spitzer raving about
Mayor Pro Tem Kelley's speech that day and he gave Mission Viejo a lot of accolades for being
on the cutting edge with its Social Host ordinance. Mayor Reardon discussed the two recent
events in the Council Chamber dealing with prescription drug abuse and she encouraged parents
to start a conversation with their children on the subject. She also noted that she attended several
recent sports league opening day events and she encouraged residents to attend the Wounded
Warriors softball game this weekend.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 9:45 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Reardon adjourned the meeting in memory of Staff Sergeant Jonathan Davis to Monday,
March 18, 2013, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of March 18, 2013

City Council Minutes  11  March 4, 2013
